set.pl: Iwers homestead, SE quarter of sec. 35 T80N R1W (Inland township), Cedar County, between Sunbury and Bennett (1936 will-trial land list)
set.st: Three bachelor brothers, William, John and Henry Iwers, owned 800+ acres in Inland township and kept their money at home. After John (1935) and Henry died, a court-ordered search of the 160-acre homestead turned up $112,600 in iron boxes under the machine shed in June 1936. In late July 1936 attorneys and Louis Voss found the last $21,000 (municipal bonds in a tobacco tin in a gunny sack) under an old Mitchell car. Over $230,000 was dug up in all; nothing was reported left.
set.t: FOUND: the hoard was recovered in 1936. Strays around the old machine shed and car site are possible but none were reported missing. Private land: ask permission first.
src: AP, Evening Star (Washington) 6 Jul 1936 and other AP copies (one wire story)
Davenport Daily Times, 22 Oct 1936, p. 12 (will trial land list; newspapers.com 302468783)
later feature "Sunbury, Iowa treasure" (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 615706, 621354, 625069)

set.pl: GNIS Palmyra; 100-acre farm "two miles northwest of Palmyra" and about ten miles NE of Indianola, on a road corner (farm not yet placed)
set.st: Andy Dickson, "the old Quaker", died aged 80 on 20 Aug 1909 at his 100-acre farm two miles northwest of Palmyra. His nephew-administrator found $2,300 in gold by an old shed about 20 yards from the house; the sheriff and a county supervisor then dug $10,005 more (a glass jar of $4,005 and an earthenware jar of $6,000) about the same shed, used as a smokehouse. The gold lay under the shed doorway; a notch in the door sill led them to dig in front of it. About $13,300-$13,800 was found in all, but officials believed over $25,000 had been buried. The house stood on a slight rise in a grove of elm and maple, the shed about thirty yards north of it, screened from the road by elms and a plum thicket. No later finds were reported. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: About half the believed total was never found. Place the farm 2 mi NW of Palmyra on a 1900s-1910s Warren County plat or the 1930s aerial (a farmstead SW of a road corner), then search the smokehouse site 30 yd north of the house and the house site. Private land: ask permission first.
src: Indianola dispatch 28 Sep 1909 (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 625235)
Des Moines Register, 31 Oct 1909, p. 25, feature with photos (newspapers.com 128404303)

set.pl: PLACEHOLDER Dixon; crash was in a wheat field on the Ted Knoll farm, eight miles southwest of Harmon (Lee Co.), not yet placed
set.st: A mail plane carrying 133 black (industrial) diamonds crashed nose-first and burned in March 1929 in a wheat field on the Ted Knoll farm, eight miles southwest of Harmon; the pilot had parachuted onto a farm about half a mile west. By 1 May 1929 all but 30 stones had been recovered by sifting; the wreck was sold for junk. No later reports of stones turning up. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: About 30 small diamonds in a plowed field; diamonds are not metal, so a detector will not find them. Low odds. The Knoll farm needs a 1920s Lee County plat. Private land: ask permission first.
src: AP, Evening Star 4 Jun 1929 (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends thread 595260)
Sterling Daily Gazette, 3 Apr 1929, p. 12, and 1 May 1929, p. 12 (newspapers.com 7930815)
